problems.question: An alkane chain has eight carbons and single bonds only. How many hydrogen atoms does it hold?
problems.explanation: Two hydrogens for each of the eight carbons is 16, plus one extra at each end: 16 + 2 = 18, giving C₈H₁₈.

problems.question: A skeletal formula is an unbranched zigzag line with four corners and two ends. Which molecule is it?
problems.explanation: Every corner and end represents one carbon, so four corners and two ends make six carbons in one straight chain: hexane.

worked.title: Hydrogens on a long chain
worked.setup: A wax molecule is a single-bond alkane chain of 25 carbons. Find how many hydrogen atoms it holds.

steps.say: How many hydrogens do the 25 carbons hold at two each?
steps.hint: Every carbon in the chain holds at least two hydrogens.

steps.say: How many extra hydrogens do the two end carbons hold combined?
steps.hint: Each end carbon is only bonded to one other carbon.
steps.explain: Each end carbon holds one extra hydrogen: 1 + 1 = 2.

steps.say: How many hydrogen atoms does the chain hold in total?
If those same 25 carbons close into a single ring, how many hydrogens do they hold?
steps.hint: Closing a ring forms one new carbon–carbon bond, costing each end carbon one hydrogen.

worked.finish: An alkane chain of n carbons holds 2n + 2 hydrogens, and closing it into a ring removes two.

problems.question: A four-carbon chain has one carbon–carbon double bond and no ring. How many hydrogen atoms does it hold?
problems.explanation: A four-carbon alkane holds 2 × 4 + 2 = 10 hydrogens. Adding one double bond uses an extra bond on each of two carbons, removing two hydrogens: 8.

problems.question: Hydrogen chloride (H–Cl) adds to ethene. Which electron pair moves first, and where does it go?

options.label: The double bond's second pair moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl
The double bond's second pair moves to the chlorine
A lone pair on chlorine moves to a carbon of ethene
A C–H bond pair moves to the hydrogen of H–Cl

problems.explanation: Chlorine pulls the H–Cl electrons toward itself, leaving hydrogen electron-poor. Ethene's exposed second pair is electron-rich and moves to that hydrogen.

problems.question: Hexane (C₆H₁₄) and 2-methylpentane (C₆H₁₄) are structural isomers. Which one boils at a higher temperature?

options.label: They boil at the same temperature

problems.explanation: Unbranched hexane chains touch neighbors over more surface area, creating stronger attractions that take more heat to break. Hexane boils at 68.7 °C, while 2-methylpentane boils at 60.3 °C.

problems.question: Which of these molecules is chiral?
problems.explanation: Carbon 2 of 2-bromobutane holds four different groups (H, Br, CH₃, and CH₂CH₃), so its mirror image cannot be rotated to match it. Every other choice has at least two identical groups on that carbon.

problems.question: Propan-1-ol (CH₃CH₂CH₂OH) and methoxyethane (CH₃OCH₂CH₃) share the same formula. Which boils higher, and why?

options.label: Propan-1-ol, because its –OH forms hydrogen bonds with neighboring molecules
Methoxyethane, because its oxygen sits in the middle of the chain
They boil at the same temperature because they have the same formula

problems.explanation: Only propan-1-ol has a hydrogen bonded to oxygen, allowing strong hydrogen bonds between molecules. It boils at 97 °C compared with 7 °C for methoxyethane, even though both have the same mass.

problems.question: Methanoic acid (HCOOH) is dissolved in water. Which hydrogen leaves as a proton?
problems.explanation: Oxygen pulls the O–H electrons tightly, and the negative charge left on –COO⁻ is shared evenly across both oxygens, so that proton leaves easily. The C–H bond is shared nearly evenly and stays intact.

problems.question: A hydroxide ion meets chloromethane (CH₃Cl). Which atom does hydroxide's spare electron pair move to?
problems.explanation: Chlorine pulls the C–Cl electrons away from carbon, leaving carbon electron-poor. Hydroxide's pair moves to carbon while chlorine leaves with the C–Cl pair as Cl⁻, completing a substitution.

problems.question: Methanol and ethanoic acid react and release water. What kind of reaction is this, and what product forms?
problems.explanation: The two molecules join through a new C–O bond while releasing water, making it a condensation reaction. The product (methyl ethanoate) is an ester.

problems.question: Poly(propene) is made from propene (CH₂=CH–CH₃). What does each repeating unit in the polymer chain look like?
problems.explanation: Each double bond's second pair opens to bond with the next monomer, turning every double bond into single bonds: –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, with nothing left over.

problems.question: A protein chain is built from 120 amino acids linked end to end. How many water molecules were released as it formed?
problems.explanation: Each amide link releases one water molecule, and 120 amino acids in a row are connected by 119 links.

worked.title: Water from a condensation chain
worked.setup: A nylon chain is built from 800 two-ended monomers linked end to end. Find how many water molecules were released, and how many links hydrolysis must break to separate every monomer.

steps.say: How many links connect 800 monomers in a row?
steps.hint: A chain always has one fewer link than monomers.

steps.say: How many water molecules were released?
steps.hint: Each link releases one water molecule.

steps.say: How many water molecules must hydrolysis add back to separate all 800 monomers?
steps.hint: Hydrolysis adds one water molecule back across every link it breaks.
steps.explain: All 799 links must be broken, taking 799 waters.

steps.say: If the chain had 1600 monomers instead, how many water molecules would it release?

worked.finish: A condensation polymer of n monomers has n − 1 links and releases n − 1 water molecules.

problems.question: Nylon is held together by amide links formed when water left. Which reagent breaks nylon back into monomers?

options.label: Hydroxide ions in water, which add water back across each link
Bromine water, which adds across double bonds
Hydrogen gas, which adds across double bonds

problems.explanation: Amide links are built by condensation (losing water), so hydrolysis reverses them: hydroxide moves to the C=O carbon and breaks the C–N bond. Nylon has no carbon–carbon double bonds for bromine or hydrogen to react with.

problems.question: A hydrocarbon has the formula C₆H₁₂ and leaves bromine water orange. What is it?

options.label: An alkene with one double bond

problems.explanation: C₆H₁₂ has two fewer hydrogens than hexane (C₆H₁₄), so it must have either a ring or a double bond. Because it left bromine water orange, it has no double bond, so it must be a ring.
